mainTopic: The pepper mill and the child's wagon (טומאה and dragging on שבת), and the start of פרק אין צדין on trapping creatures on יום טוב
overview: This amud has two short משניות that close the פרק, and then the opening of a new פרק. A pepper mill can become טמא for three reasons, and a ברייתא matches each reason to one part of the mill: the bottom holds, the middle sifts, and the top is metal. A child's wagon can get מדרס טומאה because the child leans on it. It may also be picked up on שבת because it is a כלי. The משנה says the wagon may be dragged only over a covered surface, since on bare ground it digs a groove. The גמרא says this follows רבי יהודה, who forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין, and not רבי שמעון. The סיפא, where רבי יהודה says a wagon only presses the earth, seems to contradict this. The גמרא answers that two תנאים report רבי יהודה's view differently. After the הדרן, the new פרק אין צדין begins: fish may not be trapped from ponds on יום טוב, but animals and birds may be taken from enclosures and fed. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל starts a general rule about enclosures, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A pepper mill can become impure for three reasons
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a pepper mill can become טמא for three different reasons: as a holding vessel, as a metal vessel, and as a sieve.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The pepper mill can become impure for three reasons. It counts as a container, it counts as a metal vessel, and it counts as a sieve.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה teaches that one pepper mill is treated as three separate כלים for the laws of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an object becomes טמא because it fits one category of כלי. The pepper mill is built from parts that each fit a different category. So each reason for טומאה applies on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: A pepper mill, a small grinder for pepper
Here it means 'can become impure,' not that it already is impure
A container, something with a space that holds things
A metal vessel, which can become impure even without a holding space
A sieve, used for sifting

steps.confusionAlert: The word טְמֵאָה does not mean the mill is already impure. It means the mill is the kind of object that can become impure.

phrases.english: can become impure because of three vessels:
and because it is a metal vessel,
and because it is a sieve.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָרֵחַיִם שֶׁל פִּלְפְּלִין, טְמֵאָה מִשּׁוּם שְׁלֹשָׁה כֵּלִים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pepper mill can become טמא under three separate categories: כלי קיבול, כלי מתכת, and כלי כברה.

steps.title: Which part of the mill matches which reason
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains which part of the mill fits each category: the bottom is the container, the middle is the sieve, and the top is the metal vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A ברייתא taught: The bottom part is impure because it is a container. The middle part is impure because it is a sieve. The top part is impure because it is a metal vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that explains the משנה by matching each of the three reasons to one part of the mill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed three reasons but did not say where each one applies. The ברייתא answers that: the bottom catches the ground pepper, the middle sifts it, and the top, where the grinding happens, is metal. Each part fits a different category of כלי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was taught,' introducing a ברייתא
The bottom part
The middle part
The top part

steps.whatToRemember: The pepper mill is three כלים in one: bottom = container, middle = sieve, top = metal vessel.

phrases.english: The bottom part, because it is a container,
the middle part, because it is a sieve,
the top part, because it is a metal vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה by matching each of the three reasons to a specific part of the mill.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bottom = כלי קיבול, middle = כלי כברה, top = כלי מתכת.

steps.title: A child's wagon: impurity, carrying, and dragging on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a child's wagon can become טמא through מדרס, may be picked up on שבת, and may only be dragged over a covered surface.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A child's wagon can become impure through treading. It may be carried on שבת. It may not be dragged except over cloths.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives three rules about a child's toy wagon: one about טומאה and two about moving it on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because a child rests his weight on the wagon, it can get מדרס טומאה. It is a real כלי, so it may be picked up on שבת. Dragging it on bare ground could dig a groove, so it may only be dragged over a covered surface.

keyTerms.meaning: A small child's wagon or toy cart
Impurity caused when a זב sits or leans on something made for that
Can be picked up and carried
Dragged along the ground

steps.confusionAlert: Here כֵלִים does not mean dishes or tools. It means cloths or similar coverings laid on the ground, so the wagon does not dig into the dirt.

phrases.notes: The child leans his weight on it, so if he is a זב he can make it impure that way.

phrases.english: and it may be carried on Shabbat,
and it may not be dragged

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child's wagon can get מדרס טומאה and may be carried on שבת, but according to the תנא קמא it may be dragged only over a covered surface.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only a wagon may be dragged
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees about dragging. He says no כלים may be dragged on the ground, except a wagon, because its wheels only press the earth down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: No vessels may be dragged, except for the wagon, because it only presses the ground down.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different view on the last rule of the משנה, about dragging the wagon on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allowed the wagon to be dragged only over a covered surface. רבי יהודה turns it around: other כלים may not be dragged, but the wagon may be dragged even on the ground. Its wheels just press the dirt down and do not move earth or dig a groove.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for
Presses down, flattens the ground without digging it

steps.whatToRemember: The argument is about dragging on שבת. The תנא קמא allows the wagon only over a covered surface. רבי יהודה allows the wagon even on the ground, because pressing earth down is not digging, but he forbids dragging all other כלים.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the key question for dragging on שבת: does the object move earth and make a groove, or does it only press the ground down?
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַכֵּלִים אֵין נִגְרָרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's last rule about dragging the wagon.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No כלים may be dragged on שבת except a wagon, because it only presses the earth down and does not dig.

steps.title: Reasons for the first two rulings about the wagon
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the reasons behind the first two rulings of the משנה. The wagon is טמא מדרס because the child leans on it, and it may be moved on שבת because it counts as a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A child's wagon can become טמא through מדרס, because the child leans on it. It may be picked up on שבת, because it has the status of a כלי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the משנה line by line. It gives a short reason for each of the first two rulings about the wagon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדרס טומאה applies to things a person leans or rests his weight on, and a child leans on this wagon as he walks. Moving it on שבת is allowed because it is a real כלי, not מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Impurity passed on by a זב leaning or putting his weight on an item
Leans on
The status of a vessel or utensil

phrases.english: And it may be picked up on Shabbat,
because it has the status of a vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲגָלָה שֶׁל קָטָן — טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס, דְּהָא סָמֵיךְ עִלָּוַיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's explanation of the משנה quoted in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wagon is טמא מדרס because it is leaned on, and it may be moved on שבת because it is a כלי.

steps.title: Why the wagon cannot be dragged on bare ground
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's wording, the גמרא learns that dragging the wagon on bare ground is forbidden. The reason is that it makes a groove, a חריץ, in the earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: It may only be dragged on top of cloths. On cloths, yes; on the bare ground, no. Why? Because it makes a groove.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads a hidden rule out of the third ruling: the wagon may not be dragged on bare ground. Then it explains why: the wagon digs a groove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'only on cloths' means bare ground is forbidden. Making a groove in the ground is like plowing, a מלאכה on שבת. This reason sets up the next question about whose opinion the משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: On top of cloths or other items, not the bare ground
Ground, earth
A groove or furrow in the ground
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינָהּ נִגְרֶרֶת אֶלָּא עַל גַּבֵּי כֵלִים.
phrases.english: And it may be dragged only on top of cloths.
What is the reason? Because he makes a furrow.
phrases.notes: A furrow in the ground is like plowing, which is forbidden on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל גַּבֵּי כֵלִים — אִין, עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the משנה, moving to the third ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dragging the wagon on bare ground is forbidden because it makes a חריץ.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this? רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the משנה follows. It answers רבי יהודה, who holds that a דבר שאין מתכוין is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי יהודה's, who said that an act done without intending the forbidden result is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא would forbid dragging just because a groove might form. It answers that this is רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person only wants to move the wagon; he does not want to dig a groove. Forbidding it anyway fits only someone who says a דבר שאין מתכוין is still אסור, and that is רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is it?
A תנא who forbids unintended forbidden results
An allowed act that may cause a forbidden result the person does not intend
Forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: דבר שאין מתכוין does not mean doing something by accident. The person does mean to do the allowed act, like dragging. He just does not want the forbidden side effect, the groove.

phrases.english: who said: An unintended act is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reason from step 6 (the groove) to figure out which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא wrote this ruling about not dragging?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה, who forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין.

steps.title: It cannot be רבי שמעון, who allows dragging
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the משנה is not רבי שמעון. He clearly says a person may drag furniture as long as he does not intend to make a groove.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were רבי שמעון: he says an unintended act is allowed. As we learned: רבי שמעון says a person may drag a bed, chair, or bench, as long as he does not intend to make a groove.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer by ruling out the other option. It quotes a משנה where רבי שמעון allows dragging furniture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון allows dragging even if a groove forms, as long as the person does not mean to make one. So he would have allowed dragging the wagon on the ground too. That leaves רבי יהודה as the only possible author.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who allows unintended forbidden results
Allowed
As we learned in a משנה
Drags
As long as, provided that

phrases.english: For if it were Rabbi Shimon,
didn't he say: An unintended act is allowed?

phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out.

phrases.english: A person may drag a bed, a chair, or a bench,
as long as he does not intend to make a furrow.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הָאָמַר: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין — מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 7's answer by showing רבי שמעון could not have said this ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה forbidding dragging on the ground follows רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה where רבי שמעון allows dragging a bed, chair, or bench as long as one does not intend to make a groove.

steps.title: The סיפא says a wagon does not make a groove
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges its own answer. In the סיפא, רבי יהודה says a wagon may be dragged because it only presses the earth down, which means it does not make a groove.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the סיפא: רבי יהודה says no items may be dragged on שבת except a wagon, because it only presses down. Because it presses down, yes, it is allowed. But a groove it does not make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a problem from the end of the same משנה. It seems to contradict what was just said about רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא was explained as רבי יהודה, forbidding the wagon on the ground because it makes a groove. But in the סיפא, רבי יהודה says a wagon only presses the earth and does not make a groove. So it looks like רבי יהודה contradicts himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Look at the last part of the משנה
Are dragged
Except for
Presses down, packs the earth

steps.whatToRemember: The רישא was explained as רבי יהודה, who says the wagon makes a groove. In the סיפא, רבי יהודה says the wagon only presses the earth, with no groove. The גמרא needs to resolve this clash.

phrases.english: No items may be dragged on Shabbat,
Because it presses down, yes, it is allowed,
but a furrow it does not make?
phrases.notes: This is the problem: the רישא assumed the wagon does make a furrow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 7's claim that the רישא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רישא, which forbids dragging the wagon on the ground because of a groove, follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the סיפא, רבי יהודה says a wagon only presses the earth and makes no groove. So he would have no reason to forbid it on the ground, which contradicts the רישא.

steps.title: Two תנאים Who Both Follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying two תנאים disagree about what רבי יהודה actually held.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between two תנאים, and both are speaking according to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 9. The first part of the משנה and the סיפא do not contradict each other, because they come from two different תנאים who each report רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree that רבי יהודה forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין. They only disagree about the facts: does a wagon make a groove? The first part of the משנה holds that it does, so dragging it is forbidden. The סיפא holds that it only presses the earth down, so dragging it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Two תנאים (rabbis of the משנה period) who disagree
According to the view of

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה still follows רבי יהודה. The two halves differ only on whether a wagon makes a groove, not on the rule of דבר שאין מתכוין.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the two תנאים argue about whether דבר שאין מתכוין is forbidden. Both agree it is forbidden according to רבי יהודה. They argue only about what a wagon physically does to the ground.

phrases.notes: The first part of the משנה is one תנא, and the סיפא with רבי יהודה's name is another.

phrases.english: and both are according to Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9 by dividing the משנה between two תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the source: the רישא and סיפא come from two תנאים with different reports of רבי יהודה's view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה is one voice, so רבי יהודה cannot both forbid dragging because of a groove and allow it because a wagon makes no groove.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two תנאים both follow רבי יהודה's rule that דבר שאין מתכוין is forbidden. They differ only on whether a wagon makes a groove.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the פרק that begins יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the פרק. It is not part of the argument. It is the traditional farewell said on finishing a פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן names the פרק by its opening words, יום טוב. It shows that the discussion of the child's wagon was the last topic of this פרק. A new פרק with a new subject starts right after.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (the formula said on finishing a פרק)

phrases.english: We will return to you, Yom Tov

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final answer in Step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק יום טוב is finished, and a new פרק begins.

steps.title: No Trapping or Feeding Fish in Ponds on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens: on יום טוב one may not trap fish from their ponds, and one may not put food in front of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not trap fish from ponds on יום טוב, and one may not put food in front of them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק, אין צדין, begins with a new משנה. Its first ruling forbids taking fish out of their ponds on יום טוב and forbids feeding them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if a person wants the fish for his יום טוב meal, catching them from the pond counts as צידה, trapping. So it is not allowed. The משנה also forbids putting food in front of them, since fish in a pond find their own food.

keyTerms.meaning: Trap or hunt (from צידה, one of the forbidden מלאכות)
Ponds or enclosures where fish or animals are kept
Food

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the theme of the whole new פרק: when catching or handling a living creature counts as צידה on יום טוב.

phrases.english: from the ponds on a Festival,
and one may not place food before them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין צָדִין דָּגִים מִן הַבִּיבָרִים בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new פרק with a new topic after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fish may not be trapped from their ponds on יום טוב, and one may not feed them.

steps.title: Animals and Birds May Be Taken and Fed
steps.stepSummary: In contrast, one may take an animal or bird out of its enclosure on יום טוב and may put food in front of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one may trap an animal or bird from enclosures, and one may put food in front of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the opposite ruling for animals and birds. They may be taken from their enclosures and may be fed on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אבל signals a contrast with the fish. An animal or bird in an enclosure is seen as already caught, so taking it is not real צידה. Since it depends on its owner like a household animal, he may also feed it.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild animal
A bird
But, however (introduces a contrasting ruling)

steps.confusionAlert: The same word בִּיבָרִים is used for both cases, yet the rulings are opposite. The difference is the creature: fish in a pond count as not yet caught, while animals and birds in an enclosure count as already caught.

phrases.english: However, one may trap an animal and a bird

phrases.notes: Here בִּיבָרִין means pens for animals and birds, not fish ponds.

phrases.english: and one may place food before them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל צָדִין חַיָּה וְעוֹף מִן הַבִּיבָרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting case to Step 12: animals and birds instead of fish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal or bird may be taken from its enclosure on יום טוב, and one may feed it.

steps.title: Not all enclosures are the same
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that enclosures differ from one another, and he begins to give a general rule for telling them apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Not all enclosures are equal. This is the general rule: Every...
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds a qualification to the משנה: you cannot treat every enclosure the same way. He then starts a general rule, which the text finishes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה drew a simple line: fish ponds are forbidden, and animal or bird enclosures are allowed. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that line is too simple, because enclosures come in different kinds. The words זה הכלל tell us he is about to give one rule that sorts all the cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא and leader of the generation, quoted here in the משנה
Enclosures or ponds where animals, birds, or fish are kept
Equal, the same
This is the general rule (a phrase that introduces one principle covering many cases)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is only talking about fish. He is saying the type of enclosure matters, so even some animal enclosures may be treated differently from what the first part of the משנה suggested.

phrases.english: This is the general rule: Every

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: לֹא כָּל הַבִּיבָרִין שָׁוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the משנה's earlier split between fish ponds (forbidden) and animal or bird enclosures (permitted). He says the type of enclosure matters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Enclosures are not all the same for the laws of trapping on יום טוב. A general rule to sort them is about to be given.
